title: Why do dogs wag their tails?
examples: Does a dog wag its tail when it is happy?
What does a slow tail wag mean?
Can dogs use their bodies to talk to people?

explain.say: Dogs use their whole bodies to talk to us.

draw.text: Why do dogs wag their tails?

items: Paws can show how a dog feels.
Ears move when a dog hears things.

explain.say: When a dog is happy, its tail might wag fast.
A slow, gentle tail wag can mean a dog is calm.
Sometimes a dog's body language changes when it is scared.
When you see a dog wagging its tail, it is talking to you.
A dog might wag its tail when it sees a friend coming home.

faq.q: Does a dog wag its tail when it is just excited about food?
faq.a: Yes, dogs can wag their tails when they are excited about food. It is a sign of general happiness.
asks: Is wagging a sign of being hungry?
Does food make a dog wag its tail?

faq.q: If a dog's tail is tucked, does that mean it is always scared?
faq.a: Tucking the tail often shows fear or feeling unsure. However, other body signs help us know for sure.
asks: What does a tucked tail mean?
Is a tucked tail always fear?

faq.q: Are there different ways a dog can wag its tail?
faq.a: Yes, the speed and height of the wag can change what the dog is trying to say. It is like a dog's word choice.
asks: Can dogs wag their tails differently?
What does a fast wag mean compared to slow?

faq.q: Can a dog wag its tail if it is just tired?
faq.a: Tiredness might make a dog move slowly, but a wag is usually about emotion, not just energy levels.
asks: Is a wag possible when tired?
Does being tired stop tail wagging?

faq.q: Do all dog breeds wag their tails the same way?
faq.a: No, different dog breeds and individual dogs can have different ways of showing their feelings.
asks: Do all dogs wag their tails the same?
Is tail wagging the same for every dog?

facts: Tail wagging is a form of canine communication.
The speed of the wag can change the meaning.
A tucked tail often signals fear or nervousness.
Dogs use many body parts to communicate feelings.

quiz.say: A dog wags its tail very fast when it sees its owner. What is the dog showing?
quiz.why: A fast wagging tail is a clear sign that the dog is feeling very happy and excited to see you.

wrong.1: Running is an action, but the wag is about feeling, not just movement.
wrong.2: Sleeping is resting, and the tail wagging shows the dog is awake and feeling something.
wrong.3: Eating is about food, but the wag shows an emotion like joy.

quiz.say: If a dog keeps its tail low and wags it slowly, what might it be feeling?
quiz.why: A slow and gentle wag usually means the dog feels relaxed and calm in the moment.

wrong.1: Anger is often shown with stiff body or direct stare, not a slow wag.
wrong.2: Fear usually makes the tail tucked close to the body, not wagging slowly.
wrong.3: Playfulness often comes with a more bouncy or energetic wag.

quiz.say: When a dog uses its ears and tail to show how it feels, what is it doing?
quiz.why: Using body parts like ears and tail is how dogs communicate their feelings to us.

wrong.1: Playing is an activity, but communication is the purpose of the signals.
wrong.2: Eating is an action, not a way of sending messages.
wrong.3: Sleeping means resting, and signals happen when the dog is awake.
